arch.label: Korean War
arch.src: President Truman, news conference, 30 Nov 1950 (American Presidency Project transcript)
arch.quote: There has always been active consideration of its use. I don't want to see it used.

arch.label: U.S. accidental bomb drop in New Mexico
arch.src: Same AP/Los Angeles Times article
arch.quote: But it didn't go off, and we don't know how serious the accident was.

arch.label: U.S. accidental bomb drop in Savannah, Georgia
arch.src: 1966 JCAE testimony (W.J. Howard) describing a complete weapon with a capsule, released 1994, per Center for Arms Control fact sheet
arch.quote: 1966 Congressional testimony were released in 1994 and revealed the weapon was indeed a complete, fully-functional bomb with a plutonium pit.

arch.label: B-52 Navigation Error
arch.src: Scott D. Sagan, The Limits of Safety, Princeton University Press, 1993
arch.quote: The lost bomber was heading directly toward the Soviet Union, and was only about three hundred miles away from Soviet airspace

arch.label: Soviet nuclear weapons in Cuba
arch.src: National Security Archive, 'Last Nuclear Weapons Left Cuba in December 1962' (EBB 449), describing Gribkov's January 1992 Havana disclosure
arch.quote: revealed their presence in Cuba in 1962 at a critical oral history conference of American, Soviet and Cuban policymakers

arch.label: A Soviet Satellite Explodes
arch.src: Sir Bernard Lovell (Jodrell Bank), writing in 1968, as quoted by Canadian Pugwash Group '20 Mishaps' list
arch.quote: led the U.S. to believe that the USSR was launching a massive ICBM attack

arch.label: Intruder in Duluth
arch.src: Scott D. Sagan, The Limits of Safety: Organizations, Accidents, and Nuclear Weapons (Princeton University Press, 1993)
arch.quote: they fully believed that a nuclear war was starting as they headed down the runway.

arch.label: ICBM Test Launch
arch.src: Scott D. Sagan, The Limits of Safety: Organizations, Accidents, and Nuclear Weapons (Princeton University Press, 1993)
arch.quote: What does appear certain, however, is that none of the senior civilians in the U.S. government had any awareness of the possible dangers involved.

arch.label: Unannounced Titan Missile Launch
arch.src: Scott D. Sagan, The Limits of Safety: Organizations, Accidents, and Nuclear Weapons (Princeton University Press, 1993)
arch.quote: The Moorestown radar operators had not been anticipating this missile launch when, suddenly, it appeared on their display screens.

arch.label: Malstrom Air Force Base
arch.src: Scott D. Sagan, The Limits of Safety: Organizations, Accidents, and Nuclear Weapons (Princeton University Press, 1993)
arch.quote: Both men suggested that the personnel in the single launch control center held the capability to fire the missiles in an unauthorized manner.

arch.label: NATO Readiness
arch.src: Scott D. Sagan, The Limits of Safety: Organizations, Accidents, and Nuclear Weapons (Princeton University Press, 1993)
arch.quote: Considerable confusion emerged on October 22 because some U.S. commanders in Europe had been directed through individual service channels to go immediately to DEFCON 3

arch.label: British Alerts
arch.src: Menaul, Countdown (1980), as described by Twigg and Scott
arch.quote: Both the Thor missile force and V-bombers were at fifteen minutes readiness.

arch.label: Moorestown False Alarm
arch.src: Scott D. Sagan, The Limits of Safety: Organizations, Accidents, and Nuclear Weapons (Princeton University Press, 1993)
arch.quote: The rest of NORAD was alerted that a missile attack might be under way

arch.label: False Warning Due to Satellite
arch.src: Scott D. Sagan, The Limits of Safety: Organizations, Accidents, and Nuclear Weapons (Princeton University Press, 1993)
arch.quote: The operators at the new Falling Leaves Laredo site could neither accurately count the number of objects detected nor identify the direction of their movement.

arch.label: The Penkovsky False Warning
arch.src: Garthoff, Reflections on the Cuban Missile Crisis (1987; seen in 1989 ed.)
arch.quote: it could have had a profound effect in greatly heightening tension in the crisis.

arch.label: U2 Flights into Soviet Airspace
arch.src: Garthoff, Reflections on the Cuban Missile Crisis (1987 first ed.; seen in 1989 ed.)
arch.quote: armed with air-to-air nuclear missiles, so an incident could have been very serious.

arch.label: Operation Anadyr (B-59)
arch.src: Alexander Mozgovoy, Komsomolskaya Pravda (1995), as described by the National Security Archive
arch.quote: about the near-use of a nuclear-tipped torpedo by the captain of B-59

arch.label: Operation Anadyr (B-130)
arch.src: Huchthausen, October Fury (2002), as described in National Security Archive EBB 75
arch.quote: Captain Nikolai Shumkov ordered the preparations of torpedoes, including the tube holding the nuclear torpedo

arch.label: U.S. mistaken order during Cuban Missile Crisis
arch.src: Same: Ota/Kyodo account of John Bordne; Tovish, Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, 2015-10-25
arch.quote: Only caution and the common sense and decisive action of the line personnel receiving those orders prevented the launches

arch.label: U.S. strategic bomber crash in Spain
arch.src: New York Times and Washington Post front pages, 20 Jan 1966, per Wikipedia; NYT 25 Apr 1966 describes 'three unarmed hydrogen bombs fell on the village'
arch.quote: front page of both the New York Times and Washington Post on 20 January

arch.label: French false alarm from weather (likely)
arch.src: Admiral Philippon, La Royale et le roi (1982), quoted in L'Opinion
arch.quote: c'était probablement celui qu’il eût jugé le plus grave

arch.label: Confusing Solar Flares and Nuclear Attacks
arch.src: Same (Knipp et al. 2016; UCAR press release)
arch.quote: prepared aircraft for war

arch.label: Vietnam War (Fracture Jaw)
arch.src: New York Times, Oct 2018, on Michael Beschloss, Presidents of War (reposted by Univ. of Chicago Atomic Age blog)
arch.quote: activated a plan in 1968 to move nuclear weapons to South Vietnam

arch.label: Vietnam War (Duck Hook)
arch.src: Seymour Hersh, The Price of Power (1983): staffer asked Kissinger whether nuclear weapons should be considered; first-hand documents released Nov 2005
arch.quote: Firsthand documentation on the highly secret Duck Hook planning finally surfaced in mid-November 2005

arch.label: DPRK shootdown of U.S. EWAC aircraft
arch.src: New York Times, 1969 (shortly after the shootdown), citing Nixon administration sources, per NPR
arch.quote: reported that there was discussion of a nuclear attack against North Korea

arch.label: Sino-Soviet conflict
arch.src: Same
arch.quote: the Soviets had asked foreign governments what their reaction would be to a preemptive attack on China

arch.label: 1973 Arab-Israeli war
arch.src: Same Time story
arch.quote: in the early phases of the war Prime Minister Golda Meir ordered the assembly and arming of 13 nuclear bombs

arch.label: False Alarm During Middle East Crisis
arch.src: Scott D. Sagan, The Limits of Safety: Organizations, Accidents, and Nuclear Weapons, Princeton University Press (citing declassified Air Force documents)
arch.quote: B-52 crews rushed to their aircraft, started the engines, and prepared for a launch.

arch.label: Soviet Missile Headed Toward US?
arch.src: Senators Gary Hart and Barry Goldwater, Report on Recent False Alerts from the Nation's Missile Attack Warning System, Senate Armed Services Committee Print, GPO
arch.quote: Four SS-N-6 SLBMs were launched from the Kuril Islands as part of Soviet troop training. One of the launches generated an unusual threat fan.

arch.label: Serpukhov-15
arch.src: Yuri Votintsev memoirs (per Wikipedia, Stanislav Petrov)
arch.quote: The incident became known publicly in 1998 upon the publication of Votintsev's memoirs.

arch.label: Able Archer-83
arch.src: Same book (Gordievsky's claim of a flash telegram to KGB stations warning of a possible US strike during Able Archer); US declassified PFIAB report released 2015
arch.quote: Gordievsky that during Able Archer 83 a “flash telegram” went to all Soviet intelligence stations warning of a U.S. alert

arch.label: Failed coup
arch.src: Chicago Tribune, 'Soviet Missile Boss Defied Coup'
arch.quote: coup plotters briefly stole a briefcase containing codes and communications equipment for launching nuclear weapons from Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev

arch.label: Gulf War: Israeli nuclear weapons
arch.src: Seymour M. Hersh, The Samson Option (Random House, 1991); NYT review by Joel Brinkley 1991-10-20
arch.quote: mobile missile launchers armed with nuclear weapons moved into the open and deployed facing Iraq, ready to launch on command

arch.label: Russian False Alarm
arch.src: Interfax, Yeltsin remarks the day after the launch (quoted by BBC)
arch.quote: I indeed yesterday used for the first time my 'black' suitcase with the button which is always carried with me
